newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Chevron mulls wildcat well in North Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Chevron mulls wildcat well in North Nigeria.

text.p: Chevron Corp's unit Chevron Nigeria Ltd said on Monday its initial survey of the Benue trough in northern Nigeria had shown prospects of oil deposits and it could drill a wildcat well in the area.

"Overall, results so far are encouraging," it said in its latest assessment made available to Reuters, adding "These point to the possibility of Chevron going into the next phase, acquisition of more siesmic lines or drilling of an early wildcat well."

Chevron Nigeria Ltd is the operator of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC)/Chevron joint venture and one of the biggest oil-producing firms in the country, where the crude is pumped from the southeastern corner.
The results raise the prospect of finding oil in the north where previous surveys have failed to yield hydrocarbons.
Cheron said its leases in the Benue trough covered three states -- Bauchi, Plateau and Taraba -- where the survey was conducted.

"Part of the work was carried through natural bushlands, farmlands," it said, adding "The survey in which about 700 kilometres of two-dimensional siesmic data were acquired commenced late October 1995 and was concluded early March, 1996."
